acceptanceCriteria: With 47k receipts and 3-5 heartbeat/renew/claim writes per minute, acquire calls bounded at 150 s each reach ACQUIRED while a member is FREE, measured with the opt-in load harness or a retained host run.

Either (a) a tail made only of heartbeat/renew receipts is accepted against the audited head, with a spec requirement proving those receipts cannot change pool membership or allocation, or (b) progress survives across bounded calls without a cross-process shared base that breaks PSR-V0-051, or a recorded design decision says why not.
A PENDING result reports retries and audit duration (the #1010 'report the wait' suggestion), or that is explicitly declined.
Tamper tests in the style of PSR-V0-053 still refuse.
body:
GitHub #1010 comment (2026-10-17 14:51Z, reporter build 55abb815, which predates the V1-1560 fix merged in 072a306f1): over 4 hours with about 47,000 receipts there were 11 ACQUIRED and 146 PENDING at the client wrapper's 150 s wait, while one member stayed FREE. Writers ran at about 3-5 fast-route writes per minute (dispatcher keepLease with 13 workers at a 300 s heartbeat, plus claims and notes).

Gap in V1-1560 (PSR-V0-050..057): the resume base lives only in one command's memory (PSR-V0-051). The first resume needs one early-stopped complete attempt plus a prefix walk, which PSR-V0-055 extrapolates to about 3 minutes at 45k receipts and load 60. A client that bounds each call to 150 s and starts a new process each time therefore never reaches a resumed round.

The reporter proposes an interim: commit against the audited head when the receipts since that head are only heartbeat or renew receipts, which cannot change pool membership or allocation.

Expected: a bounded acquire call at 45k receipts completes, or returns a retryable result that lets the next call make progress. Related: V1-1569 (45k qualification), V1-1570 (store file count).
title: pool acquire: bounded client calls (150 s) exit before the first resume base exists, so the V1-1560 resume never helps them; heartbeat/renew-only tails could commit against the audited head (GitHub #1010 follow-up)
